title: Arete-27B: open-weighting a Qwen3.8-27B fine-tuned for Western values

documents.content: Nous post-trained Alibaba's Qwen3.8-27B (a Chinese open model) to reinforce Western values on it, and is releasing the result, Arete-27B, as open weights on Hugging Face. The weights, the Propaganda_Eval (803 prompts across seven value categories), and the 28,886-example training dataset (arete-data-pairs) are all published. Result: fact score rose 2.32 to 2.98/5, propaganda-containing answers fell from 22% to 1% — in line with Western models tested. No capability regression (Hermes Bench 65.60% vs base 65.77%, Terminal-Bench-2.1 70% vs 67%). The thesis: the bias layer in a Chinese-aligned model is shallow; the values in any open model are one fine-tune away; users deserve optionality in which values they work with.

The US government has taken concrete steps to restrict Chinese AI models (especially DeepSeek) from federal use, while issuing broader warnings about risks of state-aligned behavior baked into Chinese open weights. Geopolitical information in a model's context can affect code quality: studies found Chinese models produce more vulnerable code when they believe they are acting on behalf of an American entity. Nous observed refusals, deflections, and CCP-framed answers on politically sensitive topics in Qwen3.8-27B before post-training; propaganda rates in the eval: Qwen3.8-27B base 22%, DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 16%, GLM 5.3 15%, versus Western models (Mistral Large 4, Gemma 4 31B, Nemotron 3 Ultra) at 0.3-0.6%, and Arete-27B at 0.6-0.9%.
